Definition: from G3784; an ower, i.e. person indebted; figuratively, a delinquent; morally, a transgressor (against God):--debtor, which owed, sinner.
BiblicalUsage: A debtor is one who owes, and the New Testament uses the word for money, for sin, and for calling. Paul says he is a debtor both to Greeks and to barbarians, to preach the gospel to all, and that anyone circumcised is a debtor to do the whole law, while Jesus teaches us to pray about our debts and our debtors together.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe every one of us is a debtor before God, and the gospel is the news that the debt was paid by another; my only fitting answer is to owe love to everyone. And the debt I owe to everyone is love, the one debt that grows the more I pay it.
